skill.name: to-prd
skill.description: Synthesizes conversation context and codebase knowledge into a structured product requirements document, then publishes it to the configured project issue tracker.
skill.summary: Create and publish a codebase-aware PRD from the current conversation.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around a slash command and label name. Neither line executes Ruby or shell code. The skill still publishes generated content without final approval, which can expose sensitive context or create an unintended issue.

remediation.issue: PRD publication occurs without final approval.
remediation.suggestion: Show the PRD, destination, and label first, then require explicit user confirmation before creating the issue.

content.user_title: Create a PRD from Your Project Conversation
content.value_statement: Important product decisions often remain scattered across conversations and code context. This skill synthesizes them into a structured PRD and publishes it to your issue tracker.
actual_capabilities: Synthesizes existing conversation context without starting a discovery interview.
Explores the repository to align the PRD with current architecture and domain terms.
Structures requirements into problem, solution, user stories, implementation, testing, scope, and notes.
Identifies high-level testing boundaries and asks the user to confirm them.
Publishes the completed PRD to the configured project issue tracker.
Applies the ready-for-agent triage label to the published issue.
limitations: Requires a configured project issue tracker and known triage label vocabulary.
Relies on available conversation and repository context, so missing decisions may remain unresolved.
Does not conduct a full requirements interview or gather new stakeholder evidence.
May need user review before publication when the conversation contains sensitive or uncertain information.

use_cases.title: Convert Feature Discussions
use_cases.description: Turn an established feature conversation into a structured PRD with user stories, scope, and technical decisions.

use_cases.title: Document Engineering Decisions
use_cases.description: Capture architecture, interfaces, testing boundaries, and repository terminology before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Prepare Agent-Ready Work
use_cases.description: Publish a detailed project issue that an implementation agent can use as its requirements source.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic PRD
prompt_templates.prompt: Create and publish a PRD from our conversation about [feature]. Use the configured issue tracker and apply the ready-for-agent label.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after a focused feature discussion has established the main problem and solution.

prompt_templates.title: Add Repository Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Synthesize our discussion of [feature] into a PRD. Review the repository for domain language and architecture, confirm testing boundaries, then publish it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the PRD must align with an existing codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Include Architecture Decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRD for [feature] using our conversation, relevant ADRs, existing interfaces, and testing precedents. Separate confirmed decisions from assumptions before publication.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for features with established architectural constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Define Complex Delivery Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce an implementation-ready PRD for [initiative]. Cover actors, edge cases, contracts, schema changes, testing boundaries, exclusions, and unresolved assumptions before publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for broad work involving several modules or user journeys.

output_examples.input: Our discussion defined an account export feature with email delivery, audit history, and administrator controls.
output_examples.output: A published PRD describing the export problem, customer solution, numbered user stories, implementation decisions, testing boundaries, exclusions, and the ready-for-agent label.

output_examples.input: Create a PRD from our invoice synchronization reliability discussion.
output: Problem Statement: Teams cannot identify failed invoice synchronizations quickly.
Solution: Add visible synchronization status, retry controls, and audit history.
Testing Decisions: Verify visible status and retry behavior through the existing integration boundary.

best_practices: Review the proposed testing boundaries when the skill asks for confirmation.
Ensure the issue tracker and ready-for-agent label are configured before invocation.
Remove secrets and sensitive internal details from the conversation before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill when key requirements still need stakeholder interviews.
Do not publish generated requirements without checking assumptions, scope, and sensitive content.
Do not expect file-level implementation plans because the template avoids unstable file references.

faq.question: Does this skill interview stakeholders?
faq.answer: No. It synthesizes the current conversation and repository context instead of starting a new requirements interview.

faq.question: What sections does the PRD include?
faq.answer: It covers the problem, solution, user stories, implementation decisions, testing decisions, exclusions, and further notes.

faq.question: Does it inspect the repository?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews relevant codebase context, domain terminology, architecture decisions, and testing precedents.

faq.question: Will it publish the PRD automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill directs the agent to publish the PRD to the configured project issue tracker.

faq.question: Which label does it apply?
faq.answer: It applies the ready-for-agent triage label to the published issue.

faq.question: Does the PRD include file paths or code?
faq.answer: It normally excludes file paths and code. It may include a short prototype excerpt when prose cannot express a decision precisely.
